seoTitle: How to Upload Files in Microsoft Teams Easily (2026)
metaDescription: Attach a file to a Teams post from the compose box, choose between a cloud file and a local upload, and know the 250 GB size ceiling before you try to send something huge.
intro: Sharing a document in a Teams channel or community doesn't need a separate trip to a shared drive. The attachment option lives right in the message compose box, next to the same formatting tools used for a normal post. This guide walks through that flow: opening a channel, composing a post, and choosing where the file comes from, cloud storage or your own device. It also covers the size ceiling Teams enforces once the file lands in SharePoint, and where to look when a shared file seems to disappear.

steps.heading: Open the channel or community you're posting to
steps.body: In the left rail, Teams groups channels under whatever community or team you belong to, each with its own set of channels you can add to. Selecting a channel opens its main feed, with three tabs across the top: Posts, Files, and Photos. That matters because Files is where anything you upload ends up permanently, not just buried in the scrollback of a conversation.

image.caption: A Teams channel open to its Posts tab, with Files and Photos as separate tabs alongside it for anything shared here.

steps.heading: Start a post and attach a file
steps.body: Click into the post composer and it expands into a full formatting toolbar: bold, italic, lists, highlighting, and a row of icons along the bottom including an emoji picker, a paperclip for attachments, and an image icon. Click the paperclip and two options appear: Attach cloud files, for something already stored in OneDrive or SharePoint, and Upload from this device, for a file sitting on your computer. In some Teams layouts this same option sits under the plus, or "Actions and apps", icon instead of a paperclip in the toolbar; look there if you don't see one. Cloud files keep everyone on the same version and skip the upload wait; a device upload makes more sense when the file only exists locally.

image.caption: The expanded post composer, with the attachment paperclip icon sitting in the row of tools below the message field.

steps.heading: Pick the file and hand it off
steps.body: Choosing Upload from this device opens your operating system's standard file browser, with the usual shortcuts down the left side: Desktop, Downloads, Documents, Pictures, plus any folders you've pinned. Navigate to the file, select it, and click Open. Attach cloud files works differently: it opens a OneDrive or SharePoint picker instead of your local disk, and inserts a link to the shared copy instead of a separately uploaded file.

image.caption: The Upload from this device flow, opening a standard file browser to select a document, image, or folder from the local machine.

steps.heading: Post it — the file lands in Files automatically
steps.body: Once the file shows up attached to your draft, finish the message and click Post. The file becomes part of that conversation, but Teams also files it into the channel's Files tab on its own, so anyone who missed the post can still find it without scrolling back through history. Keep an eye on size if you're moving something large: files posted to a channel are stored in that channel's SharePoint library, and Microsoft's current per-file ceiling there is 250 GB, up from the 100 GB limit older guides still quote.

steps.heading: Skip the post: upload straight to the Files tab
steps.body: Click the Files tab at the top of the channel to see everything shared there in one list, sorted the way a folder would be. This is also where you'd upload a file directly, without wrapping it in a post, which suits building a shared reference library more than sharing something inside an active conversation.

troubleshooting.problem: "Attach cloud files" doesn't appear, or fails when you click it
troubleshooting.cause: Cloud attachment relies on SharePoint being enabled for your Microsoft 365 tenant. If an admin has turned it off, or your account has no SharePoint license, Teams can't reach OneDrive or the team's document library.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask your Teams or Microsoft 365 admin to confirm SharePoint is enabled for the organization. Upload from this device still works regardless of that setting.

troubleshooting.problem: A large file won't finish uploading
troubleshooting.cause: Files posted to a channel go into that channel's SharePoint library, which currently caps individual files at 250 GB. Very large transfers can also time out in the browser well before that limit.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the file size, and if it's within the cap, try again from the desktop app instead of a browser tab, or split the transfer into smaller pieces.

troubleshooting.problem: You know a file was shared but can't find it in the conversation
troubleshooting.cause: Scrollback only shows the message it was originally attached to, and busy channels bury that fast.
troubleshooting.fix: Open the Files tab instead of searching the feed. Every file shared in that channel, however it was originally attached, lives there in one list.

faq.question: Where is the attach-file button in Teams?
faq.answer: Inside the message compose box, in the row of icons below the text field. Look for the paperclip; in some Teams layouts it sits under the plus, or "Actions and apps", icon instead.

faq.question: What's the difference between Attach cloud files and Upload from this device?
faq.answer: Attach cloud files pulls something already saved in OneDrive or SharePoint, keeping everyone on the same synced version. Upload from this device opens your local file browser for a file that only exists on your computer.

faq.question: Is there a file size limit?
faq.answer: Files posted to a channel go into that channel's SharePoint library, and Microsoft's current limit there is 250 GB per file. Your organization's overall storage quota can still run out before you hit that number.

faq.question: Where do files I share in a channel end up?
faq.answer: Alongside appearing in the post itself, they're automatically filed into that channel's Files tab, which sits next to Posts and Photos at the top of the channel.

faq.question: Can I upload a file without writing a post?
faq.answer: Yes. Going directly to the Files tab lets you upload files into the channel's shared library without attaching them to a specific conversation post.

faq.question: Why don't I see the option to attach a cloud file?
faq.answer: That option needs SharePoint enabled for your organization's Microsoft 365 tenant. If an admin has switched it off, only Upload from this device will work.
